title: rollout-headroom-exec-summary-q3-2026
summary: One-page snapshot of projected GPU headroom and KV cache footprint for the Q3 model rollout. Produces three operational scenarios (fast ramp, measured ramp, deferred warmup) with concrete delta to available tokens/sec and estimated storage for KV caches. Intended for Eng Infra leads and Product rollout owners to decide reservation vs. burst strategy.
key_metrics: Baseline fleet: 2,400 A100-80GB equiv. GPUs across NA/EU/APAC
Current avg util: 62% overall (70% peak regional pockets)
Model memory profile: 110B FP16 -> 28GB host + 18GB KV working set per active shard
Avg requests/session: 24 tokens per call, 1.8 calls per session, median seq len 512
scenarios: Fast ramp (customer accepts immediate GA; onboarding concurrency multiplier x6 during first 72 hours): peak headroom exhausted in EU and US-W within 18 hours. KV warmup will produce a one-time write amplification of ~1.9x for persistent caches and needs 3.2TB ephemeral per region to prefetch hottest shards.

Measured ramp (staged rollout at 20% weekly increments with canary throttles): headroom consumption steady, system stays under SLA if autoscale burst lanes (reserved + spot) are enabled; KV warmup spread reduces instantaneous storage need by ~70%.

Deferred warmup (on-demand KV population only): reduces immediate storage pressure but increases cold latency for early users; safe for capacity-constrained regions but risks QoE spikes and higher tail latency.
Fallback plan: route low-priority traffic to quantized-compatible model variant (x2 lower mem) to relieve KV pressure while preserving 80% of output quality for non-sensitive workloads.
assumptions: New model 110B is loaded as 4 shards per GPU slot on our serving runtime with persistent KV shards stored on nvme-backed volumes
Autoscaling can add up to 20% additional capacity per region (burst pools), but lead time is 30-45m for cold start under current infra scripts
KV caching heatmap follows historical onboarding patterns: 45% of unique keys account for 85% of hits within first 48 hours
Network egress for KV sync estimated at 0.25x of persistent store size during warmup window (replication and prefetch)
risk_highlights: EU region shows <10 GPUs headroom — single large customer spike could breach latency SLOs
Warmup write amplification may temporarily saturate regional NVMe write queues, increasing request latency for unrelated workloads
Spot capacity reliance in APAC introduces preemption risk; plan must include fast-failover to hosted or reduced-quant models
recommendations: Immediate: carve 40 GPUs (global) as 'staging-reserve' for first 72 hours to smooth the fast ramp. Prefer reassigning from us-east burst pool where headroom is highest.
Medium: enable staged KV prefetch for top-10% request patterns and cap background prefetch rate to 150 MB/s per region to avoid NVMe saturation.
Long: schedule a Dedicated capacity order for EU (+12 GPUs) and migrate lower-priority backfills to quantized variant to free up host RAM for KV hot shards.
Operational: add a telemetry flag to track 'kv-warmup-io' per-node and page it at 60% of observed nvme write IOPS during rolling onboard.
cost_estimates: Fast ramp incremental GPU-hours (72h): ~6,400 GPU-hours across regions -> ~$192k (on-demand blended)
KV ephemeral storage during warmup (fast ramp): ~9.6TB write -> estimated $3.4k in storage I/O and replication costs
Reserve plan (40 GPUs reserved monthly) delta: ~$110k/month but reduces burst bill volatility and lowers 95th percentile tail costs
author_notes: This is a compact working snapshot — numbers are derived from sampled telemetry (Jan-Feb 2026) and a micro-benchmark of the new model. Please cross-check with SRE on NVMe write limits and with Sales on expected customer ramp pacing before approving a dedicated purchase. Next revision will add a per-customer allocation simulation matrix.
